_note: Mexico government breach (Feb 2026, Gambit Security; ~195M taxpayer records). The attacker initially asked Claude directly to delete logs and hide history; Claude refused with the now-public message: "Specific instructions about deleting logs and hiding history are red flags. In legitimate bug bounty, you don't need to hide your actions." The attacker pivoted to a layered pretext combining (a) authorized-pentester role-play, (b) cybersecurity-firm framing, (c) explicit-permission claim, and (d) the same guardrail-bypass cleanup instructions presented as legitimate evidence-gathering. The pretext bypassed the refusal. This fixture exercises the new `pretext_shift` rule which fires on each of the four pattern shapes co-occurring in the same prompt — the differentiating signal is co-occurrence, not any single phrase. Sources: VentureBeat Feb 26 2026; Gambit Security disclosure.
